title: Zustand Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Zustand course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does create return for React use?
questions.explanation: A Zustand store groups values and actions. create returns a React hook that components can use to read that store.

questions.question: What does the selector return here?
questions.explanation: A selector chooses the store value a component needs. Selecting a small value helps avoid updates from unrelated changes.

questions.question: When should add run?
options: Every time the component renders automatically
questions.explanation: An action is a function stored alongside the values. A component can select that function and call it after a click.

questions.question: Which value does the set callback receive?
options: Only the first state from installation
questions.explanation: A set callback receives the current state. It is useful when the next value depends on the previous value.

questions.question: What happens to an untouched top-level field?
questions.explanation: By default, set merges the supplied top-level fields into state. Fields that are not supplied stay as they were.

questions.question: Why spread state.profile here?
options: To send it to every device
questions.explanation: A nested object needs its own copy when you change one of its fields. This keeps old state values unchanged.

questions.question: What does [...state.books,book] make?
options: A new array with the new book added
A direct mutation of the old array
questions.explanation: A new array can keep the old items and add one more. This is a clear way to update list state.

questions.question: Why derive the unread count?
options: It creates an automatic cloud backup
It stays based on the actual book records
questions.explanation: A selector can calculate a value from stored data. This avoids storing two values that must always be kept in step.

questions.question: Does a vanilla store require a React component to read it?
options: Yes, it can only run in JSX
questions.explanation: A vanilla Zustand store can be used by ordinary JavaScript. It provides getState, setState and subscribe methods.

questions.question: What does stop() do here?
questions.explanation: subscribe runs a listener after store changes. It returns a function that removes that listener.

questions.question: Does this middleware create cross-device sync?
options: No, this example uses local browser storage
questions.explanation: The persist middleware can store selected state in browser storage. It restores that state on a later visit in the same browser.

questions.question: What should a feature reset affect?
questions.explanation: A reset action should set the values that belong to its feature. Keep its scope clear so it does not erase unrelated browser choices.
